newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania's resurgent right wing forms coalition.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania's resurgent right wing forms coalition.

text.p: Lithuania's victorious right-wing parties, spearheaded by independence leader Vytautas Landsbergis, signed an agreement on Wednesday to form the Baltic state's first coalition government.

The coalition between Landsbergis's Homeland Union and the Christian Democrat Party will only take office after President Algirdas Brazauskas names a candidate for prime minister, expected soon after parliament's first sitting on November 25.
Landsbergis led the resurgent right-wing to triumph in recent elections, sweeping the former Communists of the Lithuanian Democratic Labour Party (LDLP) out of power.
It was a sweet victory for the man who was most associated with Lithuania's struggle for independence from the former Soviet Union in 1990-91, only to be ousted by the LDLP in 1992.
The coalition has 86 seats in the 141-seat parliament, a comfortable majority.

"It (the agreement) is a new stage in the maturing of parliamentary democracy, which in itself does not mean that we know how to work in a coalition," Landsbergis told a news conference. "We must learn to work in a coalition."

The new right-wing government is expected to keep Lithuania on its path of integration with the West but there are some question marks over its economic policy, particularly the idea of unpegging the litas currency from the dollar.
Landsbergis confirmed the coalition would on Thursday propose Homeland Union board chairman Gediminas Vagnorius as prime minister during a meeting with Brazauskas.
Landsbergis himself is expected to become parliament speaker and prepare for a fight for the presidency in 1998.
